- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- After a price spike, model often continues upward; if sentiment turns negative or neutral, apply mean reversion by lowering forecast 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for risk aversion bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 7-day moving average as baseline and adjust ±2% based on recent volatility.
